correctness.rationale: From the exact scalar plant solution and integral cost, differentiating gives \(J'(k)=\frac12(1-\frac{1+a^2}{(k-a)^2})\) and \(J''(k)=\frac{1+a^2}{(k-a)^3}>0\). Normalization gives \(F_t(y)=y+t(y^{-2}-1)\) for \(y>0\). The unique global critical point \(y=(2t)^{1/3}\) yields \(\min F_t=\frac32(2t)^{1/3}-t\); strict positivity is equivalent to \(t<3\sqrt3/2\). Positive two-cycle equations imply \(t=2p^2/s\) and \(s^2=2p(p+1)\), hence \(p>1\) and \(t^2=2p^3/(p+1)\). This last function rises strictly from one to infinity, establishing existence and uniqueness for \(t>1\). The multiplier simplifies to \(M=5-8p+8/(p+1)\), strictly decreases, and equals minus one at \(p=(\sqrt{113}-1)/8\). SymPy verifies identities and radical exact witness (\(p=9/8\), \(M=-4/17\)). The strict hyperbolic boundaries only are classified; no unsupported global-attraction assertion or extrapolation from finite checks.

originality.rationale: The same-policy-gradient source Bu et al. (arXiv:2006.09178v1) provides gain-dependent sufficient stabilizing/descent steps but no exact all-gain scalar positive-map threshold or an attracting fixed-step two-cycle. Mohammadi et al. (TAC 2022) prove convergence at sufficiently small sublevel-dependent steps, without classifying large steps or two-cycles. Fazel et al. (PMLR 2018) concern discrete-time LQR, a different objective. published-finding corpus alias/formulation searches and available own ledgers did not show dominating/equivalent coverage. These are real inspected scope comparisons, not a proof of universal uniqueness; unindexed equivalent one-dimensional rational-map work remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: The cost is a natural and motivated scalar continuous-time feedback-control objective from the foundational LQR policy-gradient literature. The proven separation between globally preserved stabilization \(0<t<3\sqrt3/2\) and failed optimization (repelling optimum and locally attracting nonoptimal cycle for \(1<t<t_*\)) directly addresses choosing a fixed learning rate. The phase boundaries and unique cycle are exact, distinct and not implied by small-step convergence. Their dependence on the plant parameter is explicit via \(\eta=2\sqrt{1+a^2}t\). The cycle-multiplier threshold and radical witness expose a dynamical mechanism; this is more than recomputing a textbook gradient or a numerical simulation. Natural limits and unproved extensions are explicit.
